description: A coordinated effort among EU member states and other technologically advanced democracies — including Japan, South Korea, and Canada — begins to formalize shared standards for AI safety evaluation and incident reporting, inspired by early frameworks from the OECD and the G7. The initiative gains momentum as a response to the lack of transatlantic alignment and the unilateral actions taken by the US, with the EU positioning itself as a convener rather than a follower. This marks the beginning of a structured, multilateral approach to AI governance that could evolve into a credible alternative to US or Chinese models.
